title: Pipeline for code in a git repository: plan, then build each slice behind two gates, with validated retries
description: For code in a git repository: Fable plans questions, Sonnet explores, and the plan splits the work into up to 6 slices. Each slice is written by Opus in its own worktree and must pass the test gate (a bugfix slice also needs a test that fails before the fix) and a fresh-context reviewer. Failing tests go back to the writer. A review's gaps first go to a fresh reviewer that keeps only the gaps that stand: confirmed gaps start a retry (the second attempt resumes the same writer, the third and last is a fresh writer on Opus); when none stand, the slice moves on to be merged. The same gap in two failed reviews in a row stalls the slice until one replan plans the missing work. Passing slices are merged into the result branch. Validation, the Opus attempt and the stall belong to the native orchestrator (the gated workflow validates and escalates too, without the stall gate); the SDK pipeline sends the gaps straight back. Work that changes no code follows the same plan and review steps in your folder.

notes: Retries (dashed) carry the failing output, or the confirmed gaps, back to the same slice. A slice gets at most 3 attempts; then it has failed for good.

Validation, the resume and the Opus third attempt are the native orchestrator's retry flow (.claude/agents/orchestrator.md step 6); the gated workflow validates (refute) and runs its last attempt on Opus (escalateLast) too. The stall and its replan_required block are native only (plan-check.mjs, review-gate.mjs).
The SDK pipeline (npm start, frozen since 0.3.0) sends the gaps straight back, up to --retries (default 2), with no validation, no Opus attempt and no stall; it replans only with --replans N.
The bugfix check is native: for a KIND: bugfix slice, verify.sh needs a changed test that fails on the base and passes now (bugfix-check.mjs).

The SDK pipeline works on code in a git repository only (src/cli.ts). Natively, work that changes no code follows the same plan and review steps in the shared folder, with no worktrees, no integrator and no commits (.claude/agents/orchestrator.md, steps 2 to 5).
